Names in Wyvern Crown
====================
NPCs refer to you using both your first and your last name in Wyvern Crown. In order for dialogues to make sense therefore, it is sensible to have both names set for your character, rather than choosing a name like "Hawk the Slayer".

Rest
====
You can rest in several areas within Wyvern Crown, although in many of them there is a chance that your sleep will be disturbed by wandering monsters, so pick your spot wisely! In any event, you must wait at least one hour before you can rest a second time (except in inns, where you can rest at any time).

If you travel using inns, you will arrive at your destination rested with your spells replenished. Inns however have a cost and are not always available.

Game Notes

Henchmen
=========
Throughout The Wyvern Crown, you will find several companions are available to you. At any time, you can have up to two of them with you. Except under specific circumstances, a henchman cannot die, but will instead respawn at the end of a battle. Respawned henchmen generally need immediate healing, whilst a henchmen that has not respawned, can instead be raised/resurrected only by use of the appropriate spell, not via healing. In addition, if you die and have at least one surviving companion within 30 feet, they will rescue you and drag you to safety, allowing you to respawn. Otherwise, you cannot respawn and will have to reload, so travelling without any companions will make the module considerably more challenging.

Henchman commands:
======================
You can shout commands at your henchmen (open chat and type the command in game). If you add the first letter of the henchman's name at the beginning, only he or she will obey the command. For example, gcome will make just Godfroy move to you, whereas come will bring all your henchmen running. Note: if a henchman is doing nothing, he probably can't hear you (out of range, deafened, etc).
====The Commands are:
come - move henchmen to the PC (this command is disabled in a couple of areas for gameplay reasons). Remove stand ground commands.
open - open the nearest lock (if it is possible)
hide - into/out of stealth mode
search - into/out of search mode
combat - attack nearest perceived enemy. It clears the stand ground command, and reapplies standard HotU combat behaviour after the first action. Note that spellcasters are more likely to use their weapons than spells when you do this.
disarm - disarm the nearest trap (if possible)
stop - puts henchman in stand ground mode
flee - flee from the enemy you are currently fighting, and remain out of combat (using stand ground) unless attacked. Use this one only in emergencies, as the direction and reliability of 'flee' is dependant on NPC facing, enemy positions, etc.

Your brother Jonas will not obey these shouted commands as he is more independantly minded than to listen to his sibling in everything!

Horses
======
In order to mount or dismount a horse that you own, select the mount or dismount option from your radial menu (which is found in class actions). Then 'target' your horse. You can tell your henchmen to mount via their dialogue, or using the radial menu to command them to mount, and they will mount any unmounted horse you have in your party.

There are several types of horses in game. Those that are trained for war can be used for battle, and you can improve your ability to fight on horseback through the available feats. If you try to use an untrained horse in battle, it is more than likely that it will flee, leaving you highly vulnerable to your opponents.

It may seem obvious, but you cannot use horses indoors. If you enter a building, your horses will be tied to the nearest hitching post. Don't forget to go and retrieve them if you need them, though if you use overland travel, the option to automatically gather horses will be offered to you (though you will travel on foot unless you opt to mount them).

Horses of course can have several advantages if used properly. Some can fight even unmounted, and if you have some of the mounted feats, you will become a powerful warrior on horseback. With packs, all horses can carry equipment. Don't overlook some of the more obvious benefits of horses too: a mounted man is quicker than one on foot and a horse is also stronger than a man. On occasion all of these benefits may have a use.
